sources.locator: Quanyu Tang, An improved lower bound on Erdős problem #962 (2025). Research note linked from the Erdős Problems page inspected (proves log k(n) >= (1/sqrt 2 - o(1)) sqrt(log n log log n)). Erdős Problem #962 page inspected: k(n) is the largest k such that some m <= n has m+1, ..., m+k each divisible by a prime > k; Erdős had log k(n) >> (log n log log n)^(1/2) and Tao proved k(n) <= (1+o(1)) n^(1/2). OEIS A327909 inspected: the smallest start of a run of n or more integers each with a prime factor greater than n is 6961 for n = 30 and 10305 for n = 31 (the sequence is nondecreasing), so the longest run starting at most 10^4 has 30 terms. For runs starting at most 10^4 the maximum is 30, so the task recovers the run 6961..6990 or an equivalent.
